source.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(\pi ,0).$
source.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy))-\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y-x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =-y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-x\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(\pi ,0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(\pi ,0)} & =-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)-\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0) \\  & =0-\pi \cdot 1 \\  & =-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=2\left(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\,j\right)$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(\pi ,0).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\right))-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\right)) \\  & =2\left(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y-x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\right)\\  & =2\left(-y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(\pi ,0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(\pi ,0)} & =2\left(-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)-\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\right)\\  & =2\left(0-\pi \cdot 1\right)\\  & =2\left(-\pi \right)\end{aligned}
$$

source.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=(x+{y}^{2})\,i+y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(0,-1).$
source.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1))-\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{{x}^{2}+1}-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(0,-1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(0,-1)} & =\frac{2(0)(-1)}{{0}^{2}+1}-2(-1) \\  & =0+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

source.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=(2x+{y}^{2})\,i+y{e}^{x}\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(1,1).$
source.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{x})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+{y}^{2}) \\  & =y{e}^{x}-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(1,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1,1)} & =(1){e}^{1}-2(1) \\  & =e-2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=9\left((2x+{y}^{2})\,i+y{e}^{x}\,j\right)$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(1,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(9\left(y{e}^{x}\right))-\frac{∂}{∂y}(9\left(2x+{y}^{2}\right)) \\  & =9\left(y{e}^{x}-2y\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(1,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1,1)} & =9\left((1){e}^{1}-2(1)\right)\\  & =9\left(e-2\right)\end{aligned}
$$

source.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=({x}^{2}+xy)\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(\frac{1}{2},0).$
source.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy) \\  & =\frac{1}{x+y}-x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(\frac{1}{2},0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1/2,0)} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2}+0)}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =2-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=2\left(({x}^{2}+xy)\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,j\right)$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(\frac{1}{2},0).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $F$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\right))-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left({x}^{2}+xy\right)) \\  & =2\left(\frac{1}{x+y}-x\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(\frac{1}{2},0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1/2,0)} & =2\left(\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2}+0)}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\\  & =2\left(2-\frac{1}{2}\right)\\  & =2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy) \\  & =\frac{1}{x+y}-x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(\frac{1}{2},0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(1/2,0)} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2}+0)}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =2-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
